The free, fast and secure Linux desktop. 

 
 lordos.org ·
 Download ·
 Features ·
 Gallery ·
 Paper ·
 FAQ ·
 Docs 
 

LordOS is a free GNU/Linux distribution based on Debian, with its own desktop environment:
a display server and Wayland compositor written in C, its own interface engine, and native apps
made to feel calm, clear and private. It runs on 64-bit PCs and on the Raspberry Pi 5, and the
Linux apps you already use (Chromium, Firefox, GTK and Qt apps) run alongside the native ones. The machines it has
been reported on (22 so far: 14 with Intel graphics, 4 with AMD, none with NVIDIA yet) are listed in
 docs/HARDWARE-REPORT.md .

 
 
 
 

 Everything you need. Nothing you don't.

 
 --- --- 
 A desktop of its own Its own display server and Wayland compositor in C and its own interface engine, on a solid Debian base. Smooth on 64-bit PCs (amd64; what it has been run on), and light enough for the Raspberry Pi 5 (arm64). 
 Private by design Installable LordOS apps run isolated and ask before using your camera, microphone, files or network. You decide. 
 A firewall you can see Watch every connection on a live world map, then allow or block it per app, by domain, address or network, and restrict camera, microphone, files and more. Subscribe to public blocklists of ads, trackers and malware, or deny everything a rule doesn't allow. 
 Passwords built in A vault for passwords, 2FA codes and cards that unlocks with a password or a USB key. 
 Mail, Calendar, Contacts Native apps for your accounts, with remote images blocked until you say so. 
 LordOS Web Runtime Web apps installed as LordOS apps, with their own window, Dock icon and unread count. Each app and each profile runs in its own sandboxed process, and the Store offers a catalog of 37. 
 Your Linux apps too Chromium, Firefox and GTK apps fit right in, with the same window frame and dark mode. 
 AI apps in the Store A curated catalog: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Visual Studio Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, goose, opencode, and llama.cpp and whisper.cpp to run models on your own computer, each from a pinned, verified source. The Store downloads over HTTPS. 
 System Information Every piece of hardware and what LordOS makes of it, a report you can read before you copy it, and checks that try LordOS's security claims on your own computer. A Performance tab runs LordBench: quick and full tests shown against reference machines, never as one score. Community hardware reports: share yours on GitHub with your own account (LordOS sends nothing); the Compatibility panel shows the accepted ones, and docs/HARDWARE-REPORT.md compares every machine reported so far (22). 
 Cleaner See what uses the disk and remove what can safely go. A scan only reads, and nothing changes until you review and confirm a plan. 
 Remote Desk One app for RDP and VNC, drawn by LordOS itself, with no client window or toolkit. Files connects to servers too: SMB, NFS, SFTP, FTP and WebDAV open as folders. 
 Moving wallpapers Short loops behind the desktop and the login screen, for a compatible GPU with hardware decoding, with no software mode. They pause when nobody sees them. 
 Disk Formats One Store item opens NTFS, exFAT, FAT, HFS+ and APFS volumes on the desktop, with every driver's license and source shown first. HFS+ and APFS are read-only. 

Measured, not promised: on the final ISO test before the first release (a 0.7.0 build, 2026-10-18) the
whole system idled at 465–487 MB of RAM , of which lord-server (the display server with the whole
desktop) was 32–36 MB , and booted in about 16 s (see docs/ISO.md , "Final ISO
test"). The released 0.8.5-beta, updated in place on a VMware VM with GPU composition, used 592 MB for
the whole system about five minutes after sign-in and showed its first frame 7.4 s after the kernel
started ( results/0.8.5-beta/vmware-fusion ). What is isolated today, exactly, is in
 docs/PRIVACY.md .

 Get LordOS

The latest release is 0.8.8.9-beta 
(2026-11-15), an update through Store → Updates and apt ; the images below are still
0.8.8-beta's (2026-11-02). Releases are signed and published on GitHub Releases
and on lordos.org. Before you download, see
what LordOS needs and
how to run it in a virtual machine.

- PC (64-bit): a live and installable ISO, lordos-live-0.8.8-amd64.iso . Try it without installing.
- Virtual machine: an OVA for VirtualBox and VMware, lordos-0.8.8-amd64.ova . Give any virtual machine at least 4 CPUs and 4 GB of memory, ideally 16 GB with many apps.
- Generic arm64 (UEFI): a live and installable ISO for arm64 machines and virtual machines,
 lordos-live-0.8.8-arm64.iso , new in 0.8.7. Tested on emulated QEMU only; this release's was built but not booted.
- Raspberry Pi 5: a ready-to-flash image for SD card or NVMe, lordos-0.8.8-rpi5-arm64.img.xz ,
 with fan control and our own kernel. The Raspberry Pi 5 and the Raspberry Pi 500 (same image) are the supported boards.
- Already running LordOS? It updates in place from the signed repository on lordos.org.

 Verify your download. SHA256SUMS is signed with the LordOS release key (Ed25519),
fingerprint c7155b8e6bbbb180f907381994d06af76d333016cd6f3facf67cadd053ea108e . See
code signing and docs/SIGNING.md .

Status: beta . See CHANGELOG.md and docs/ROADMAP.md .

 Documentation

- docs/README.md : the index of every document.
- The paper ( docs/PAPER.md ): vision, architecture,
 security model, performance and roadmap, with links to the source files.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md : components, processes and dependencies.

 Repository map

- server/ : lord-server (display server and Wayland compositor: DRM/KMS and evdev straight
 from the kernel, without X11, libdrm or libinput) plus lord-sessiond , lord-netd ,
 lord-netperm , lord-fand and the sandboxed helpers ( lord-media , lord-doc , lord-vault ,
 lord-maild , lord-fetch , lord-tls , lord-clean , lord-lan , lord-rdesk , lord-screencast ,
 lord-tts , lo
